task_instance: Created a small sample Node.js/TypeScript repo (package.json with express + @sentry/node deps, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, Dockerfile) inside the work directory, ran the skill's Phase 1-3 detection commands (find for indicator files, dependency inspection, existing settings/.mcp.json check), and generated a Phase 4 recommended .claude/settings.json permissions file following the skill's baseline + stack-specific + package-manager-exclusivity rules.
evidence: Sample repo at sample-repo/ with package.json (express, @sentry/node deps), package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, Dockerfile. Ran `find . -maxdepth 2 (...)` which correctly listed Dockerfile, package-lock.json, package.json, tsconfig.json. Ran `cat package.json`, `cat .claude/settings.json` (none), `cat .mcp.json` (none) per Phase 2/3. Generated sample-repo/.claude/settings.json with baseline read-only commands plus Node-specific (node --version, npm list/view/outdated since package-lock.json present), TypeScript (tsc --version), and Docker (docker --version/ps/images) entries, deliberately excluding yarn/pnpm commands per the package-manager exclusivity rule. Verified with `python3 -m json.tool .claude/settings.json` -> 'VALID JSON' and confirmed zero occurrences of 'pnpm'/'yarn' in the file. This reproduces the skill's core deliverable (a generated settings.json permissions recommendation from repo analysis) end-to-end using only local shell commands, no network or credentials required.
